ShortDescription.Value: Real timetables for public transport — fixed departures, auto-sized fleets and terminus timing points. Works for buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and planes.

Publish.LongDescription:
Turn any public-transport line into a scheduled service. Works for every passenger type: buses, trams, trains, metros, ferries and aircraft.
Per line you opt in and set:
- a first departure time and peak / off-peak / night intervals (the peak windows are configurable), - the mod then DERIVES how many vehicles the line needs to hold that headway, and raises the game's vehicle-count ceiling so the derived fleet is never clamped, - a terminus stop (timing point) where early vehicles are held to the scheduled departure, and where surplus vehicles retire — after finishing their loop and dropping passengers, not mid-route.
Select any stop to open a printed-timetable departure board for every line that serves it, listed from the first departure of the day. Day-only and night-only lines only show and run the intervals that apply to them, and a night line is scheduled inside the night window.
No timetable set = the line runs exactly like vanilla. Everything is controlled from the line's own info panel plus a floating departures board.
OPTIONAL SETTINGS (all off by default — a plain timetable needs none of them):
- "Realistic travel time" (free): the game's own loop estimate is optimistic (it ignores the time buses lose braking and accelerating at every stop), so posted times drift ahead of reality. Turn this on and the mod measures each line's REAL loop as it runs and posts realistic stop times, so early buses wait at each stop until their true departure. It warms up — for the first day or two it still shows the estimate while it measures, then switches each stop to the measured time. - "Provision fleet for real travel time" (increases number of vehicles): also sizes each line's vehicle count to its real loop. A line whose real loop is ~2x the estimate needs about twice the vehicles to hold the same headway. Grow-only and capped. - "Stop at every stop (even empty ones)" (free): by default a bus skips a stop where nobody boards or alights, so that stop isn't held to schedule; the terminus is now always honoured, and this extends that to every stop. Lines run a little slower. - "Minimum stop time" for buses and for rail: how long a vehicle stands at a stop when it arrives on time or late, so passengers have time to board. Buses 2 minutes, rail 5 by default — a train or metro exchanging a full platform takes far longer to load than a bus, and the game's travel estimate ignores boarding time entirely. A longer stop means a longer real round trip, so the line will ask for more vehicles to hold the same interval. - "Realistic Trips / slow-time compatibility" (ALPHA): keeps timing correct if you run a mod that lengthens the in-game day (Time2Work / Realistic Trips). Leave off otherwise.
CLEAN UNINSTALL: Options has a "Remove all mod data from this save" button. It reverts every line to the base game and deletes the mod's data from your city, so you can uninstall with nothing left behind. It clears your timetables, so it asks first — and after confirming, let the game run for a moment before you save.
Recommended: for accurate timetables at no cost, turn on "Realistic travel time" and leave the rest off; add "Provision fleet" only if you want the mod to also buy the buses that headway really needs.
KNOWN ISSUES:
- "Vehicles no longer un-bunch after removing the mod." The mod writes two values into a line's save data — an "unbunching factor" (an early pre-v0.2.3 build), and a "vehicle interval" it uses to size the fleet. If you remove or disable the mod WITHOUT first switching a line's timetable off, those values can stay frozen in the save (the base game never resets them), so vehicles leave a stop immediately without spacing out. FIXED as of v0.3.2.2: the mod now repairs both automatically on load, for every line, and safely — the vehicle interval is rebuilt from the line's own settings, so a count you set by hand with "Assigned Vehicles" is preserved. To repair an affected save: subscribe to v0.3.2.2 (or newer), load your city, then save. Normal unbunching returns, and you can keep or remove the mod afterwards.
Source (open source, MIT): https://github.com/AmicusDeus/TransitTimetables
Localized into 11 languages (German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese-BR, Russian, Chinese Simplified & Traditional). Translations are machine-generated — corrections welcome.
Made with Claude Code's Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 models.
Publish.ChangeLog:
v0.4.0 [BETA] — Missed trips, saved travel times, station stop times, and a clean uninstall
This release is marked BETA on purpose: it is a large change to how vehicles are retired and dispatched, and it has been reviewed line by line but NOT played through in a long test. Please report anything odd on GitHub and I will turn it around quickly. If a change misbehaves you can step back: "Minimum stop time" for rail can go back to 2, "Manage vehicle count" hands vehicle counts back to the base game, and the master switch pauses the whole mod without uninstalling.
- NEW: MISSED TRIPS ARE NOW CAUGHT UP. If a scheduled departure passes with no vehicle at the terminus (traffic, or the game dropping a new vehicle onto the middle of the route), the next vehicle to arrive used to cancel that trip and wait for its own next slot — so on a long headway you got several vehicles parked at the terminus while the line ran empty. It now makes a brief stop and departs to cover the gap instead, but only when the next scheduled departure is still far enough away that leaving now cannot bunch the two together. (Reported by a community member — thank you.)
- NEW: MEASURED TRAVEL TIMES ARE SAVED WITH YOUR CITY. "Realistic travel time" learns each line's true round trip by watching it run. Those measurements used to live only in memory, so every time you quit they were lost and each line spent a day or two re-learning from scratch. They are now stored in the save and come back instantly on load, which also means vehicle counts are correct from the first minute instead of drifting while the line re-measures.
- NEW: "Minimum stop time" for buses and for rail (Options > Stops). How long a vehicle stands at a stop when it arrives on time or late, so passengers actually have time to board. Buses default to 2 minutes (unchanged). RAIL DEFAULTS TO 5 MINUTES — this is a deliberate change: a train or metro exchanging a full platform takes far longer to load than a bus, and the game's own travel estimate ignores boarding time entirely, which is a large part of why rail lines really take much longer than the game predicts. A longer stop means a longer real round trip, so a rail line will ask for more vehicles to hold the same interval. Set it back to 2 if you prefer the previous behaviour.
- NEW: "Remove all mod data from this save" button (Options > General). One press reverts every line to the base game and deletes the mod's data from your city, so it can be uninstalled with nothing left behind. It clears your timetables, so it asks first. After confirming, let the game run for a moment before you save.
- FIX: a vehicle could retire at a stop SHARED with another line while nothing of its own line was there to take the next departure. The mod checked whether "a vehicle" was at the terminus without checking it belonged to the same line, so another line's bus counted as cover. It now only ever counts its own. (Reported by a community member — thank you.)
- FIX: vehicles could DISAPPEAR MID-ROUTE instead of finishing their loop. The mod protects a vehicle the game wants to retire so it can carry its passengers to the terminus first, but that protection was skipped whenever a line was already at its target count — and in that state the game retired vehicles wherever they happened to be. The protection now runs in every state, while still standing aside when the game is legitimately shutting a line down (a day-only line at night, or a line you set inactive) so those lines still empty out properly.
- FIX: lines could shed vehicles BELOW their target. Vehicles marked for retirement stayed marked after the line was no longer over target, so more of them retired than the line could spare. The list is now rebuilt as the target changes.
- FIX: several smaller fleet issues — the mod and the game could disagree about a line's target count right after loading and pull against each other; the per-line vehicle safety cap now applies on every path (and is set high enough that it never limits a legitimate long line); and a diagnostic message that repeated every few frames is now throttled.
v0.3.5 — Optional "Manage vehicle count" toggle, so a dedicated fleet mod can own vehicle counts instead.
v0.3.4 — Localized into 11 languages. Machine-translated, community corrections welcome.
v0.3.3.2 — The departures board now shows a line's custom name instead of its number.
v0.3.3 — Fixed long waits at ordinary stops for vehicles the game drops onto the middle of a route; added a master on/off switch that pauses the mod without uninstalling; removed the built-in achievements toggle.
v0.3.2.2 — Auto-repair for leftover vehicle-interval data that stopped vehicles un-bunching after the mod was removed. Subscribe, load your city, save.
